summary: Sends and receives raw data over TCP/IP as either a client or server, logging received bytes, lines, or read chunks and sending through Python or Tscript methods.

key_params.name: mode
key_params.note: Communicate as TCP client or TCP server

key_params.name: address
key_params.note: Server IP or host when this operator is a client

key_params.name: port
key_params.note: Network port to listen on or connect to

key_params.name: shared
key_params.note: Share a connection with other networking DATs using the same protocol

key_params.name: format
key_params.note: Append one row per byte, per line, or per last socket read

key_params.name: callbacks
key_params.note: Callback DAT executed once for each received message

key_params.name: executeloc
key_params.note: Choose the execution context for received-data callback scripts

key_params.name: fromop
key_params.note: Operator path used when Execute from is set to Specified Operator

key_params.name: maxlines
key_params.note: Maximum number of received message rows to retain

key_params.name: bytes
key_params.note: Output raw bytes in a separate column

key_params.name: customext
key_params.note: Custom editor extension when extension mode uses a custom extension

common_gotchas: TCP/IP is stream-based; in One For All Received Data mode, message boundaries are arbitrary socket read chunks.
Per Line mode does not log until newline, carriage return, or null termination arrives.
This DAT captures messages without queuing or buffering beyond its output table, so Python callbacks may need to assemble protocol frames.
Client mode requires the remote server address; server mode listens on the configured port.
Windows firewall can block connections even when port and address parameters are correct.
key_concepts: TCP/IP DAT sends and receives data over a TCP connection as either client or server.
Received data can be appended by byte, line, or socket read chunk, which affects row boundaries.
Callbacks are the official path for handling incoming messages while class methods send data.
Firewall, port, address, and client/server mode must align before a connection can exchange data.
